text:
Alex: Heads-up — helm upgrade for model-serving v2 got stuck in post-upgrade hook on prod-cluster-3. Release is `redwood-models/v2` and deploy bot shows `HOOKS FAILED` :warning:

Marta: ugh. Which hook? post-upgrade job? any logs?

Alex: Yeah, post-upgrade Job `init-affinity-check` never started pod. kubectl describes shows Pending with reason `0/5 nodes are available: 5 node(s) didn't match nodeSelector` — job has nodeAffinity to gpu-pool. We scaled GPU pool but nodes weren't Ready during hook window.

Sam: Can you paste the helm status? DeployBot just posted: `DeployBot: helm upgrade redwood-models v2 --namespace models returned non-zero exit code (hook failed)`.

Alex: here's the job yaml snippet from chart hooks: ```yaml
metadata:
  annotations:
    "helm.sh/hook": post-upgrade
    "helm.sh/hook-weight": "0"
    "helm.sh/hook-delete-policy": hook-succeeded
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      nodeSelector:
        cloud.google.com/gke-accelerator: nvidia-tesla-v100
      tolerations:
        - key: "gpu"
          operator: "Exists"
      containers: [ ... ]
```

Jen: nodeSelector + strict tolerations = will never schedule to non-gpu nodes. If autoscaler hasn't added nodes yet, Job will stay Pending and helm will wait until timeout.

Marta: Are we running helm with --wait? I think CI pipeline calls helm with `--wait --timeout 3m`. That window is too short for gpupool scaleup sometimes.

Sam: Also ArgoCD/Flux will try to reconcile chart vs manifests while helm hook job is pending — can create a race where GitOps kills/rewrites the hook resource between helm retries. That can break helm's internal hook lifecycle.

Priya: Quick mitigation: manually scale nodepool or patch job to relax nodeSelector so it can run on any node as fallback. We can also change hook to be non-blocking (move work to a controller or post-deploy async task) so helm upgrade doesn't block entire release.

Alex: I manually patched the job to remove nodeSelector and added toleration fallback. Pod started and job completed. Helm release finished afterwards. But we have to fix chart.

Marta: Agreed. Proposed long-term fixes:
- Move heavy scheduling checks out of blocking helm hooks (prefer pre-upgrade or sidecar controller)
- Add fallback toleration/nodeAffinity policy so hook can run on control plane nodes in emergencies
- Increase helm --timeout in CI for GPU rollouts or make rollout pipeline sequential for GPU charts
- Add a leader-lock/annotation in GitOps so Argo doesn't delete helm-managed hook resources mid-hook

Sam: Technical suggestions for chart change: make the Job use `nodeAffinity.preferredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution` instead of required, set `activeDeadlineSeconds` and `backoffLimit` to avoid indefinite waits, and keep `helm.sh/hook-delete-policy: before-hook-creation,hook-succeeded` so stale jobs are cleaned up predictably.

Jen: Also add an admission check in CI: if chart contains required nodeSelector for GPU, the pipeline should ensure gpupool has >= N Ready before running helm. Could be a terraform output check or small k8s readiness probe.

Priya: I'll open a PR to change the hook to preferredDuringScheduling + add activeDeadlineSeconds=900. I'll also add a CI gate to check gpupool size before GPU-chart releases.

Alex: I'll follow up with SRE to tune autoscaler/scale-up speed and possibly prewarm a small buffer of GPU nodes during heavy release windows.

Marta: For immediate postmortem, please add the incident notes to #incidents and link the failing helm release logs. We need the exact timestamps so we can correlate autoscaler events.

DeployBot: Note: release `redwood-models/v2` was marked failed at 2029-04-01T18:12:57Z. Hook job `init-affinity-check` created 2029-04-01T18:11:03Z, pod scheduled 2029-04-01T18:15:12Z after manual patch.

Sam: Action items:
- Priya: PR -> chart changes (non-blocking/fallback affinity) (ETA: today EOD)
- Alex: SRE follow-up on scale-up speed and temporary prewarm (ETA: tomorrow)
- Marta: CI change to increase timeout or gate on gpupool readiness (ETA: next sprint)
- Jen: Add GitOps reconciliation note to avoid hook races (we may add `argocd.argoproj.io/sync-wave` or similar)

Priya: tagging @marta @alex for PR review once it's up. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:

Alex: Thanks — good catch on the affinity pattern. Lesson: blocking hooks that assume fast infra changes = brittle.

Jen: closing loop: once PR merged we'll run a canary release to staging with the new hook config and confirm helm doesn't block when gpupool scales slowly.

Priya: Will post the PR link and staging results here.
